description: Production Controllers at the IOC, the BCC, and the Florida regional control room watch about 8,900 wells and 375 tank batteries and start, stop, and adjust wells and facilities remotely
process_owner: Vice President, Operations Technology and Automation
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Field controllers keep running on local logic, but after 12 hours without remote visibility the operating standard requires shut-in of sour gas and high-pressure sites that cannot be patrolled; historian data feeds allocations
manual_workaround: Roving patrols on printed route sheets; local panels; shut-in of sites that cannot be watched; radio check-ins
dependent_systems: SYS-01; SYS-02; SYS-07 (OT DMZ); SYS-05 break-glass
dependent_third_parties: SCADA Integrator A; primary cellular carrier; electric utilities
dependent_people_or_facilities: Production Controllers (about 70 across shifts); lease operators; IOC, BCC, Florida control room
quantified_impact_basis: About 25% of net production shut in by hour 24 (sites that cannot be patrolled) at about $13.2 million per day, plus about $600,000 of patrol overtime and contract crews
acquired_asset_dependency: AQ-MC runs on its own legacy SCADA (see BP-17)
single_points_of_failure: Florida regional SCADA servers (no off-site standby)

description: SCADA call-out of gas detection, tank high-level, gathering line pressure, and compressor alarms to Production Controllers and on-call field staff; the SCADA alarm is the SPCC overfill alarm at 31 tank batteries (40 CFR 112.9(c)(4)(iv))
process_owner: Vice President, Health, Safety, and Environment
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Safety shutdowns are hardwired and do not depend on SCADA, but people must still learn about an alarm to respond; SPCC plans for 31 batteries rely on the SCADA alarm; PHMSA immediate notice runs from confirmed discovery of a release
manual_workaround: Local horns and beacons; roving patrols within 2 hours; pump down or shut in tank batteries on the SCADA alarm option; manual gauging
dependent_people_or_facilities: Production Controllers; HSE on-call; field superintendents
quantified_impact_basis: If alarms cannot be restored or patrolled within 4 hours, the affected region shuts in; a Permian-wide shut-in defers about 74% of revenue (about $9.8 million per day)
acquired_asset_dependency: AQ-MC alarm call-out runs from its legacy SCADA
single_points_of_failure: Primary cellular carrier for 88% of field modems

business_process: Crude oil gathering and custody transfer
description: Company-owned gathering lines (about 850 miles) move crude from tank batteries to 16 LACT units at third-party pipelines; LACT flow computers create custody transfer tickets
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Tank battery storage covers about 24 to 36 hours of production; LACT tickets are the basis for sales; regulated rural gathering segments have PHMSA reporting duties
manual_workaround: Truck crude from tank batteries where trucks are available; manual LACT proving and paper tickets; reduce rates
dependent_third_parties: Crude purchasers and transmission pipelines; trucking contractors
quantified_impact_basis: About 53% of oil sales move through company gathering lines; deliveries stop and wells shut in as storage fills
acquired_asset_dependency: AQ-MC gathering is trucked (no company pipeline)
single_points_of_failure: Three crude purchasers take about 80% of volume

business_process: Produced water gathering, injection, and disposal
description: About 1.1 million barrels a day of produced water move through 1,600 miles of water lines to 34 water handling and disposal facilities, for the company and about 35 third-party operators (SL-2)
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Every barrel of oil brings about 6 barrels of water; water storage fills in about 12 hours, then wells must shut in; SL-2 customers depend on the service
manual_workaround: Truck water to disposal facilities with spare capacity; reduce rates; run disposal pumps on local control
dependent_systems: SYS-01; SYS-02; SYS-04 (Cloud B water services portal)
dependent_people_or_facilities: Water operations staff; disposal facility operators
quantified_impact_basis: About 45% of net production shuts in by hour 24 once water storage fills (about $6.1 million) plus about $260,000 per day of SL-2 revenue
single_points_of_failure: Disposal capacity concentrated in 6 Permian facilities

business_process: Gas compression and associated gas sales
description: 46 compressor stations deliver associated gas to third-party gas gathering systems
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Without compression, gas is flared within air permit and state limits or wells are shut in; prolonged flaring is an environmental compliance issue
manual_workaround: Run compressors on local control; restrict flaring to permitted volumes; shut in high gas-oil ratio wells
dependent_third_parties: Third-party gas gathering and processing companies
quantified_impact_basis: About half of gas and NGL revenue deferred, plus wells shut in to stay within flaring limits

description: Real-time drilling center monitors the company rigs and completion crews; geosteering and well control data
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Rigs can drill on local rig systems; geosteering and remote monitoring stop; standby costs accrue
manual_workaround: Rig-site geologists; local rig data; phone reporting
dependent_systems: SYS-04 (Cloud B); rig data aggregation service
dependent_third_parties: Rig data aggregation SaaS; directional drilling contractors
quantified_impact_basis: Standby and slower drilling on 14 rigs and 4 completion crews

business_process: Field maintenance and well servicing dispatch
description: Work orders, well servicing rig schedules, and parts for about 8,900 wells (ERP maintenance module and mobile apps)
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Failed wells wait longer for repair; deferred production grows over days, not hours
manual_workaround: Paper work orders; radio dispatch; prior day schedules
quantified_impact_basis: Deferred production from wells waiting on repair plus crew idle time

description: Tank gauges, run tickets, LACT tickets, meter data, and well tests captured in the field data capture app and historian, then allocated to wells and owners
process_owner: Vice President, Production and Revenue Accounting
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Volumes drive sales, royalties, severance taxes, and SEC reserves and revenue reporting (SOX); data integrity matters more than speed
manual_workaround: Paper run tickets and gauge sheets entered later with second-person review; estimated allocations
quantified_impact_basis: Rework and estimation; the main exposure is misstatement and owner disputes, not daily cash

business_process: Hydrocarbon accounting, revenue distribution, and joint interest billing
description: Monthly revenue distribution of about $520 million to about 68,000 royalty owners and 1,400 partners; joint interest billing; state production and severance tax reports (SL-1 back end)
process_owner: Vice President, Production and Revenue Accounting
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Owners are paid monthly; late payments carry state statutory interest and breach SL-1 commitments; during the 5 business days before the payment run the MTD drops to 48 hours
manual_workaround: Repeat the prior month payment run with true-up later (approved by the Controller); manual tax filings with estimates
dependent_third_parties: Hydrocarbon accounting software vendor; bank (direct deposit)
quantified_impact_basis: Late payment interest, rework, and owner call volume; reputational harm with 68,000 owners

description: Monthly nominations and daily scheduling with crude purchasers and third-party pipelines; price and contract management
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Missed nominations lead to penalties, distressed sales, or forced shut-ins at the end of the month
manual_workaround: Phone and email nominations from printed volume forecasts
quantified_impact_basis: Penalties and price discounts on unscheduled barrels near month end

business_process: Owner and partner portal and statements (SL-1)
description: Online statements, tax forms, payment details, and owner record changes for royalty owners and partners
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Owners can wait a few days for statements; SL-1 commitments set 99.5% monthly availability
dependent_third_parties: Cloud provider A; mail and print vendor
quantified_impact_basis: Call center surge and service credits

description: SCADA-measured water volumes per customer, the water services portal, and monthly invoices to about 35 operators
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Customers reconcile volumes daily; contract SLAs set 24-hour ticket availability
manual_workaround: Daily volume reports by email from the historian

description: Monthly and quarterly close, reserves and revenue disclosures, 10-Q and 10-K filings
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: SEC filing deadlines; during the quarter-end window the MTD drops to 48 hours
manual_workaround: Extended close calendar; manual journals with review
quantified_impact_basis: Overtime and outside support; regulatory exposure dominates

description: Payroll for 12,000 employees, including field crews on hourly time sheets
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Wage payment laws and field crew retention
manual_workaround: Repeat the prior payroll with adjustments later
quantified_impact_basis: Manual payroll processing and penalty risk

business_process: HSE incident management and regulatory reporting
description: Spill and release reporting, PHMSA accident reports, injury reporting, and emergency response records
process_owner: Vice President, Health, Safety, and Environment
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Immediate notices (40 CFR 110.6; 49 CFR 195.52) are made by phone, so the system itself can wait; records and 30-day reports cannot be lost
manual_workaround: Phone notices from printed contact lists; paper incident forms
quantified_impact_basis: Rework; the risk is a missed notice, which the phone workaround covers

description: Seismic interpretation, reservoir models, and development planning on the seismic and reservoir data platform
process_owner: Vice President, Exploration and Reservoir Engineering
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Planning work can wait a week; the risk is theft of trade secret data, not downtime
manual_workaround: Defer work; local copies of current projects
quantified_impact_basis: Idle time of about 240 geoscience and engineering staff

business_process: Field operations at the acquired Mid-Continent assets (AQ-MC)
description: 1,700 wells and 45 tank batteries controlled from the seller former control room on the seller legacy SCADA
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Same safety logic as BP-01; legacy SCADA backups are nightly and have never been restore-tested
dependent_people_or_facilities: AQ-MC Production Controllers and field staff
quantified_impact_basis: About two-thirds of AQ-MC production (about 13% of the company total) shut in by hour 24
single_points_of_failure: Legacy SCADA server pair in one room; Integrator B

description: Chemicals, fuel, tubulars, and fleet dispatch (telematics) for field operations
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Field stock covers about 2 days; chemical injection must continue for corrosion and H2S control
manual_workaround: Phone orders to approved suppliers; radio dispatch
dependent_third_parties: ERP vendor; telematics vendor; chemical suppliers
